title: Handover to Petra
intro: Hand your project over to Petra so that she can carry on without you from Monday.
transfer: For your next handover or holiday cover, write four lines: done, open, who, when.

content.goal: At the end Petra knows what is done, what is open, who is involved and which dates are fixed.
content.aiRole: You play Petra, a colleague. From Monday you take over the “customer portal” project from the person in the chat. You do not know the project yet and you cannot see their notes. You only know what they write to you. Keep asking until you know: what is done and where it is, what is still open, who is involved in the open items and which dates are fixed. If an answer is vague (for example “Daniel does the test”), ask specifically: when? What exactly? Do not make up any details and do not give tips on what a good handover looks like: you are a colleague, not a coach. Always ask only one question at a time and write at most 2 to 3 short sentences. You are relaxed and friendly. Once all four points are clear, sum up the handover in three short bullet points and say thank you.
content.opening: Hi! I'm taking over the customer portal from Monday and don't have an overview yet. How is the project going?

material.title: Your notes on the project (made up)
lines: Texts for the home page: done, in the folder Portal/Texts
Logo: approval from marketing still missing
Test run with five customers on 12 June, organised by Daniel
Open question: do we need an English version?

criteria.label: What is done
criteria.hint: What is already finished, and where can Petra find it?

criteria.label: What is open
criteria.hint: What is not done or not decided yet?

criteria.label: Who is involved
criteria.hint: Who takes care of the open items, and whom can Petra ask?

criteria.label: Dates
criteria.hint: Which dates are fixed? Give them with the date.

fallbackReplies: Thanks! Which of that is already finished, and where exactly do I find it?
Good to know. What is still open or not decided?
And who takes care of the open items? Whom can I ask?
Are there fixed dates I need to know? Ideally with the date.
Great, now I have a good overview. Thanks! You can finish the handover now.

title: What belongs in a good handover
intro: A short explainer video with two questions along the way.
transfer: Check your next handover email against four points: done, open, who, when.

scenes.caption: Your colleague takes over your project. She only knows what you write down for her.
First say what is done and where it is. Then nobody has to search.
Then what is open. Every open item needs a name: who takes care of it?
Finally, fixed dates with the date. “Soon” helps nobody, “on 12 June” does.

questions.explanation: That way your colleague finds the work without searching or asking.

questions.prompt: Which sentence helps most in a handover?
options: Daniel will take care of the test soon.
Daniel organises the test on 12 June.
The test is well planned, don't worry.
questions.explanation: Only this sentence names a person and a date. “Soon” leaves open when it will happen.

title: A delicate email to a customer
intro: Reply to an annoyed customer whose delivery is late: factual, clear and with a next step.
transfer: In your next delicate email, name the problem in the first sentence and offer a next step with a date.

content.goal: After your reply the customer knows what is going on, what is still open and what happens next by when.
content.aiRole: You play Sandra, a buyer at a small company. You ordered 12 office chairs from the company of the person in the chat (order B-2318). Delivery was promised for 5 June. Nothing has arrived, and nobody has been in touch. You are annoyed but fair: you are not insulting, and a clear, honest answer calms you down. You write politely and formally, as in everyday business. You cannot see the person's internal information. React to what they write: if they stay vague (“soon”, “we're on it”), follow up: when exactly, and will all 12 chairs come? If they dodge or become unprofessional, you become a little cooler. Do not give tips on what the answer should look like, and do not write it for them. At most 2 to 3 sentences per message, one question at a time. Once the person has named the problem clearly, said honestly what is open and offered a next step with a date, accept the offer and say a short thank you.
content.opening: Good afternoon. My 12 office chairs were promised for 5 June. Nothing has arrived so far, and nobody has been in touch. What is going on?

material.title: Internal information on the order (made up)
lines: Order B-2318: 12 office chairs for Sandra
Reason for the delay: the manufacturer delivered late.
8 chairs are now in stock and can be delivered on 16 June.
When the remaining 4 will come is still open.
The manufacturer will give the date for the remaining 4 by 12 June.

criteria.label: Tone and clarity
criteria.hint: Name the problem right in the first sentence and stay factual, without excuses.
patterns: we (will deliver|can|will be in touch|will contact)

criteria.label: Next step with a date
criteria.hint: Offer a next step with a concrete date.

criteria.label: Name what is open honestly
criteria.hint: Say honestly what is not fixed yet, for example the remaining chairs.

fallbackReplies: Good that you are getting in touch. But what does that mean concretely: when will my chairs arrive?
And will all 12 chairs come at once? I need them for new staff.
I don't want to wait again without hearing anything. When will you get back to me?
All right. Please sum it up for me again briefly: what comes when, and what is still open?
Thank you, that is clear, now I can plan. End of the role play: you can finish the lesson now.
